jobs.title: Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Number: R0251517

Environmental Analyst

The Opportunity:

Provide environmental support throughout the lifecycle of the program. Work closely with environmental subject matter experts, state, and USG environmental entities on planning, design, and construction. Design, implement, and monitor environmental control systems to maintain regulatory and company environmental standards. Apply advanced skills, extensive technical expertise, and full industry knowledge. Develop innovative solutions to complex problems. Work without considerable direction. Mentor and supervise team members.

Join us. The world can't wait.

You Have:

5+ years of experience with environmental compliance
5+ years of experience with NEPA analysis
Experience supporting environmental impact assessments, site investigations, remediation projects, environmental constraints assessments, permitting activities, and conceptual site model development
Experience using environmental information, GIS data, mapping resources, and project data to identify environmental constraints, ecological sensitivities, access considerations, and project risks
Ability to manage competing requirements
Ability to come up with creative and innovative solutions
Ability to provide schedule management and development for long-term projects
Ability to obtain a Secret clearance
Bachelor's degree or 7+ years of experience working in the environmental field in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

Experience working environmental assessments with the USG
Experience working environmental assessments at a USG Launch Test Range or Spaceport
Experience working NEPA and CEQA in the State of California
Experience analyzing monitoring, survey, laboratory, and site investigation data, preparing technical summaries and interpretations to support project decision-making
Ability to work well in a fast-paced environment with multiple stakeholders

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

Compensation

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $77,600.00 to $176,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

Identity Statement

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy

AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your
own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided
.

Work Model

Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.

Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.
Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen or customer facility, in alignment with your leadership's expectations and the needs of the role.
Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed full-time at a customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, status as a protected veteran or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, local, or international law.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe waste is more than management, it’s also an opportunity to innovate. As part of our Waste sector, you’ll help shape solid waste infrastructure and environmental stewardship. With a top-tier industry ranking, our team delivers comprehensive solutions that span waste planning, remediation, engineering and implementation. You’ll collaborate closely with clients and communities to design sustainable, cost-effective systems that contribute to cleaner environments and healthier communities. This isn’t just a job; it’s a chance to drive meaningful changes in the waste industry and build a legacy of sustainability.

Primary Responsibilities

The successful candidate will provide environmental complaince support for Alaska solid waste projects but could also be assigned to projects in other market sectors in and outside of Alaska. Specific responsibilities will include:

Conduct field work: groundwater sampling,surface water sampling, and landfill gas monitoring and sampling.
Support solid waste permit applications, including writing and reviewing technical work products (environmentat documents and technical studies).
Work with project managers, clients, and subject matter experts for permitting needs.

Candidates must demonstrate a commitment to exemplary quality standards for professional practice and deliverables. Candidates must have field work experience and be able to work safely and efficiently in remote outdoor settings in Alaska under a variety of weather conditions. Candidates must be able to work cooperatively with professionals from other disciplines, clients, project managers, business development professionals, and operational leadership. This is a full-time position based in Anchorage, Alaska.

Preferred Qualifications

2 to 5 years environmental permitting and/or compliance experience in Alaska
Experience with field sampling, monitoring, solid waste/landfill, and air quality
Preference given to local candidates

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Sciences or closely related field
Knowledge of wetland delineation, field investigation techniques, and agency coordination requirements
Excellent writing and communication skills
MS Office experience
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications. We have over thirty manufacturing and assembly plants worldwide servicing over 10,000 customers in more than 100 countries. Worldwide headquarters are located in Reading, PA, USA with regional headquarters in Europe and Asia. We complement our extensive line of Motive Power and Energy Systems with a full range of integrated services and systems. With sales and service locations throughout the world, and over 100 years of battery experience, EnerSys is the power/full solution for stored DC power products.

Motive Power applications include industrial lift trucks and pallet jacks, rail equipment, mining equipment, and airline ground support equipment. Some of the motive power brands include Hawker, Ironclad, General Battery, and Fiamm. Wherever there is a need for motive power, EnerSys offers the perfect energy solution.

Job Purpose

Provide technical environmental support to all company personnel. Monitor environmental regulations and provide technical support to location personnel to ensure compliance with federal and state environmental regulations/standards. Implement and monitor the company's environmental management system. Works with and maintains "confidentially"
in the handling of employee and business information.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Prepares required reports to regulatory agencies (Environmental Protection Agency, Missouri Department of Natural Resources, Department of Transportation, and City of Warrensburg). Maintains all related records and documentation. Interact both verbally and in writing with above listed agencies on a regular basis.
Overall responsibility to assure that the ISO 14001 EMS is effectively implemented and maintained. Acts as EMS Management Representative or designee to ISO 14001 registrar.
Responsible for air quality program activities including permitting, monitoring control devices, and identifying problems/issues with environmental protection systems.
Gather and document pertinent environmental data.
Responsible for hazardous waste management activities including registration, identification, transportation, disposal, auditing, SPCC program and training.
Supervision and direction of the hazardous waste handler.
Evaluates all new and existing pollution control equipment requirements. Develops specifications and recommends improvements and changes as required. Completes and submits environmental permits to regulatory agencies as required.
Advises plant facility maintenance personnel regarding pollution control and treatment systems and assists in operations and maintenance as required.
Responsible for ensuring required environmental monitoring and sampling is conducted in compliance with regulatory standards.
Responsible for implementing and maintaining technical programs for skill-based employees (i.e. fall protection, Control of Hazardous Energy, Confined Space, and Hot Work).

Supports the implementation and monitoring of all other EHS programs as required.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s Degree in safety/environmental management or similar degree and/or 3 years of relative work experience.

Language Skills: Fluent verbal and written skills in English. Effective interpersonal communication skills a must.

Mathematical Skills: High level of accuracy in basic math and use of 10 key calculator.

Reasoning Ability: Ability to associate cause and affect relationships and determine patterns of activity in anticipation of change to the operation or personnel.

Computer Skills: Must have strong intermediate Microsoft Office skills.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Visual Emission Certification, Hazardous Waste Certification, HAZWOPPER, ISO 14001 Lead Auditor.

Other Skills and Abilities: Must be able to multi-task with attention to detail. Self-starter and takes initiative.

General Job Requirements

Generic

jobs.title: Remediation Lead,
jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Baxter, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $112,000 - $154,000 annually. The estimated salary is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. This position may also be eligible for discretionary bonuses. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

US Benefits At Baxter (except For Puerto Rico)

This is where your well-being matters. Baxter offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical and dental coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Baxter US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Baxter

Equal Employment Opportunity

Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal

Reasonable Accommodations

Baxter is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities globally. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information.

Recruitment Fraud Notice

Baxter has discovered incidents of employment scams, where fraudulent parties pose as Baxter employees, recruiters, or other agents, and engage with online job seekers in an attempt to steal personal and/or financial information. To learn how you can protect yourself, review our Recruitment Fraud Notice.

AI Disclaimer

Baxter may use AI-enabled technologies to support portions of the hiring process, such as scheduling or skills matching. Final decisions regarding candidate applications and selection are made by our hiring teams, who review any AI-assisted outputs before decisions are made, and we remain committed to fairness, inclusion, and thoughtful decision-making led by our hiring teams throughout the selection process. Our AI-enabled technologies do not automatically disqualify candidates or make hiring decisions.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
new_jobs.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions for industrial applications. We have over thirty manufacturing and assembly plants worldwide servicing over 10,000 customers in more than 100 countries. Worldwide headquarters are located in Reading, PA, USA with regional headquarters in Europe and Asia. We complement our extensive line of Motive Power and Energy Systems with a full range of integrated services and systems. With sales and service locations throughout the world, and over 100 years of battery experience, EnerSys is the power/full solution for stored DC power products.

Motive Power applications include industrial lift trucks and pallet jacks, rail equipment, mining equipment, and airline ground support equipment. Some of the motive power brands include Hawker, Ironclad, General Battery, and Fiamm. Wherever there is a need for motive power, EnerSys offers the perfect energy solution.

Job Purpose

Provide technical environmental support to all company personnel. Monitor environmental regulations and provide technical support to location personnel to ensure compliance with federal and state environmental regulations/standards. Implement and monitor the company's environmental management system. Works with and maintains "confidentially"
in the handling of employee and business information.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Prepares required reports to regulatory agencies (Environmental Protection Agency, Missouri Department of Natural Resources, Department of Transportation, and City of Warrensburg). Maintains all related records and documentation. Interact both verbally and in writing with above listed agencies on a regular basis.
Overall responsibility to assure that the ISO 14001 EMS is effectively implemented and maintained. Acts as EMS Management Representative or designee to ISO 14001 registrar.
Responsible for air quality program activities including permitting, monitoring control devices, and identifying problems/issues with environmental protection systems.
Gather and document pertinent environmental data.
Responsible for hazardous waste management activities including registration, identification, transportation, disposal, auditing, SPCC program and training.
Supervision and direction of the hazardous waste handler.
Evaluates all new and existing pollution control equipment requirements. Develops specifications and recommends improvements and changes as required. Completes and submits environmental permits to regulatory agencies as required.
Advises plant facility maintenance personnel regarding pollution control and treatment systems and assists in operations and maintenance as required.
Responsible for ensuring required environmental monitoring and sampling is conducted in compliance with regulatory standards.
Responsible for implementing and maintaining technical programs for skill-based employees (i.e. fall protection, Control of Hazardous Energy, Confined Space, and Hot Work).

Supports the implementation and monitoring of all other EHS programs as required.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s Degree in safety/environmental management or similar degree and/or 3 years of relative work experience.

Language Skills: Fluent verbal and written skills in English. Effective interpersonal communication skills a must.

Mathematical Skills: High level of accuracy in basic math and use of 10 key calculator.

Reasoning Ability: Ability to associate cause and affect relationships and determine patterns of activity in anticipation of change to the operation or personnel.

Computer Skills: Must have strong intermediate Microsoft Office skills.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Visual Emission Certification, Hazardous Waste Certification, HAZWOPPER, ISO 14001 Lead Auditor.

Other Skills and Abilities: Must be able to multi-task with attention to detail. Self-starter and takes initiative.

new_jobs.title: Remediation Lead,
new_jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.
